_comment: v1 roster. Armor is millimeters of effective thickness by facing: front / left / right / rear / top — five facings, as docs/decisions/0004 and docs/design/rules.md have specified since they were written. Left and right carry the same number today; they are separate keys so that the day a unit is asymmetric it is a data change and not a code change. Penetration is millimeters at 1000 m and falls off with range through combat.pen_falloff_per_100m. Shred is the per-hit armor degradation on a non-penetrating hit. Accuracy is a per-gun multiplier on combat.base_hit_chance. Ammo overrides combat.default_ammo. Optics is the base spotting range in meters for a stationary unit in the open, before terrain concealment, movement and exposure are applied.
_optics_note: The optics were 1400 / 1150 / 900 m against maps whose measured median clear sightline is about 141 m (docs/decisions/0020), which meant range never bound and the light tank's optics advantage was invisible. Iteration 2 picked, and picked the terrain: these are sighted so that concealment and movement land effective ranges inside the band the maps actually offer. A stationary tank in heavy woods (x0.25) goes unseen until 80-125 m; one sprinting across the open is seen as far as line of sight reaches.
_assault_note: The wave attacker's tank — 2g. Deliberately worse than everything else on every axis but numbers: armor under the light tank's, penetration that needs a flank or the rear even against the medium, and the poorest optics on the roster, so the attacking mass advances half-blind into defenders it cannot see. Its mp sits between light and medium — the waves must arrive, not trickle.
